overview: Harden the existing Linux automation scripts for Zotero and a mounted WebDAV folder, with the main synchronizer remaining automatic while failures become testable and explicit.
goals: Keep the main Zotero/WebDAV synchronization path automated once configured.
Make the main synchronizer import-safe so unit tests can exercise helpers without secrets or live API calls.
Add narrow tests around configuration, path, cache, copy, rename, and failure-reporting behavior.
Ensure critical failures are visible in logs, final reports, and process outcomes.
nonGoals: No conversion of support scripts into separate products.
No cross-platform support beyond Linux with mounted WebDAV in the current cycle.
No live Zotero API calls in unit tests.
No manual confirmation prompt in the normal main sync path.
successMetrics: The main sync module can be imported without required environment variables or a mounted WebDAV folder.
Unit tests cover the first hardening seam without contacting Zotero.
Syntax validation passes for all observed Python scripts.
Final reports and exit behavior distinguish critical failures from successful sync completion.
openQuestions: Whether future integration tests should use a fake Zotero server or real opt-in credentials.
Whether the repository should later adopt a package layout after hardening the script boundaries.

stack.hosting: Local Linux automation with mounted WebDAV
stack.database: No database; local JSON hash cache under ~/.cache/zotero_sync_webdav
stack.auth: Zotero API key from environment or env file

importFormat.description: Not applicable. The project processes local PDFs and Zotero API responses rather than importing a user-provided data file.

rules: The main synchronizer remains automatic by default.
Missing secrets, missing WebDAV mount, copy failures, rename failures, and API failures must not be reported as successful sync completion.
Unit tests must not require ZOTERO_API_KEY, a live Zotero account, or a mounted WebDAV folder.
Filesystem mutation helpers must not overwrite existing destination files silently.
Each Ralph cycle executes exactly one story.

stories.title: Make main sync import-safe and testable
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want zotero_sync_webdav.py to be import-safe so tests can exercise pure helpers without secrets, a mounted WebDAV folder, or live Zotero calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Move required-environment validation and runtime-only side effects out of module import and into an explicit runtime path used by main().
Importing zotero_sync_webdav with no ZOTERO_* environment variables does not raise and does not contact Zotero.
Example: a unit test can import normalize_filename, normalize_aggressive, resolve_target_folder, and _coerce_response_items without a .env file.

Negative case: calling the runtime config loader with missing ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID, ZOTERO_API_KEY, or ZOTERO_SYNC_TARGET_FOLDER returns or raises a clear configuration failure before any Zotero API call.
Add a tests/ suite using the Python standard library unittest module for import-safety, path resolution, filename normalization, and malformed Zotero response coercion.
The quality gates pass: python3 -m py_compile zotero_sync_webdav.py zotero_mirror_collections_to_obsidian.py and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

stories.title: Test filesystem mutation helpers
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want copy, rename, and hash-cache helpers covered by temporary-directory tests so file mutation behavior does not regress silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Add unit tests for rename_webdav_file covering successful rename and existing-destination collision.
Add unit tests for copy_to_local_storage covering copied, exists, and copy-failure outcomes without touching the real ~/Zotero/storage directory.
Add unit tests for hash cache lookup and cache entry rename using temporary files.
Example: renaming a WebDAV PDF to an unused canonical name updates the path and cache entry.
Negative case: when the destination filename already exists, the helper does not overwrite it and returns the original path.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Add automated preflight checks
stories.description: As an unattended automation user, I want preflight checks to catch missing Linux/WebDAV and local-storage prerequisites before the sync starts mutating Zotero or files.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a preflight function for required config values, WebDAV folder existence, WebDAV readability, local storage writability, and optional desktop tooling availability.
The preflight keeps the main sync automatic; it fails fast with a clear error instead of asking for confirmation.
Example: a mounted readable WebDAV directory and writable local storage allow the sync to proceed.
Negative case: a missing target folder stops before Zotero attachment creation or file rename/copy operations.
Add unit tests for pass and fail preflight cases using temporary directories.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Make run outcome truthful
stories.description: As an operator, I want the script's final report and process result to clearly distinguish completed syncs from critical failures.
acceptanceCriteria: Define critical failures for missing config, failed Zotero connection, missing target folder, failed attachment add, failed copy when required, and unexpected processing exceptions.
Ensure main() returns an explicit status or exits nonzero for critical failure while preserving a successful zero-exit path for completed runs.
Example: when Zotero connection fails, the final output records the failure and the process exits nonzero.
Negative case: a run with zero PDFs in an existing target folder exits successfully and reports no work rather than failure.
Add tests for success, no-work, and critical-failure outcome mapping without live Zotero calls.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Rclone timeout resilience and hashing bypass
stories.description: As a user, I want the sync script to bypass or quickly skip stalled file hashing on the rclone mount so the sync completes within 1 hour.
acceptanceCriteria: Reduce the remote file read/hash timeout from 180s down to a much lower threshold (e.g. 15s to 30s) so multiple stalled files do not consume the 1-hour harness execution window.
Ensure that files that time out are explicitly skipped and logged without aborting the entire sync process.
Provide a short-term memory or 'quarantine' list of files that timed out recently so subsequent sync passes do not retry them endlessly before processing new files.
If possible, bypass hashing for already-known matched files relying on mtime and size, skipping the full content hash on every run.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Orphaned file recovery pass
stories.description: As a user, I want the sync script to safely recover and materialize the 291 missing orphaned Zotero PDF attachments to the drive without mixing them into the standard heavy synchronization loop.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a dedicated recovery pass or sub-command to handle rematerialization of Zotero PDFs that are known by the API but completely missing from their expected drive path.
Ensure the recovery ignores already-synchronized files.
Add unit tests for the recovery logic.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Add test coverage for folder deduplication and single-instance locks
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want the recently added folder deduplication and single-instance lock features to be covered by unit tests to prevent silent regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Add unit tests for preprocess_drive_duplicate_folders covering identical and missing PDFs.
Add unit tests for ensure_single_instance covering successful lock acquisition and lock collision.
The quality gates pass.

stories.title: Present sync status in the existing Zotero extension
stories.description: As an operator, I want the existing Zotero Sync Recognizer extension to open a local read-only status panel from the Zotero menu so I can see current progress, the latest outcome, errors, and duplicate-review work without opening logs or changing the automated sync.
acceptanceCriteria: Keep zotero_sync_recognizer as the only extension and preserve its ping, recognize, import, discard, and fallback behaviors.
The synchronizer atomically writes a local JSON status snapshot at startup, during PDF processing, on successful completion, and on terminal errors without contacting a new service.
The extension adds a Zotero menu action that opens one reusable status panel and polls only that local snapshot while visible.
The panel shows idle/running/failed/completed state, processed versus total PDFs, errors, duplicate blocks/review work, and the latest completion time.
A missing or malformed snapshot is shown as an explicit unavailable state; opening the panel never starts, stops, or modifies a sync.
Unit tests cover snapshot contents and failure states without a live Zotero API call; JavaScript syntax validation covers the extension source.

stories.title: Maintain a recent-PDF Zotero Web cache
stories.description: As an operator, I want the normal WebDAV synchronizer to keep a bounded copy of my most recently added readable PDFs in a private Zotero group so they remain readable on zotero.org without modifying the complete primary library.
acceptanceCriteria: Enable the cache only when a configured private group ID is present; the primary library, its WebDAV files, and local copies remain immutable from the cache path.
Select eligible primary-library PDFs by descending dateAdded and a configurable 270 MiB default budget, skipping unavailable local copies and individual files too large for the budget.
Create cache-only records in the group, upload their PDFs through group Zotero Storage, and remove only previously marked cache-only records that fall outside the selected set.
Failures in the cache path are explicit in the final report but never delete source-library records or make the core WebDAV reconciliation destructive.
Unit tests cover recency selection, byte-budget boundaries, unavailable files, and cache-only deletion planning without live Zotero calls.

stories.title: Quarantine and audit trail for duplicate file removal
stories.description: As the owner of the PDF library, I want every duplicate PDF the sync removes to go to a local quarantine with an audit record, so a wrong duplicate decision can be undone instead of losing the file.
acceptanceCriteria: A quarantine_file() helper copies the file into ~/.cache/zotero_sync_webdav/quarantine/<YYYY-MM-DD>/, verifies size and SHA-256 of the copy, and only then removes the original; on any failure the original stays in place, the partial copy is removed, and the helper reports failure.
Each successful quarantine appends one JSON line to ~/.cache/zotero_sync_webdav/duplicate_actions.jsonl with timestamp, action, original path, kept path, SHA-256, reason, and quarantine path.

The three code paths that delete duplicate PDFs with os.remove (delete_redundant_webdav_duplicate, Obsidian redundant-copy dedup, and folder-dedup same-hash removal) go through quarantine_file(); a failed quarantine means the file is not deleted and the case is logged as a failure.
Quarantine date directories older than 30 days are purged at the start of a normal sync; only directories matching YYYY-MM-DD under the quarantine root are ever removed.

Unit tests cover: successful quarantine with manifest line, rollback leaving the original intact when removal fails, purge keeping recent and non-date directories, and delete_redundant_webdav_duplicate preserving the canonical file while quarantining the redundant one.
py_compile and the existing test suite show no new failures versus the pre-change baseline of 17 failing tests.
stories.notes: Zotero item deletion (zot.delete_item) is deliberately out of scope; it moves to US-011 with the Zotero trash flag.

stories.title: Read-only duplicates report and safer Zotero item removal
stories.description: As the owner of the library, I want a read-only report that classifies duplicates by content hash against Zotero collections, and I want bibliographic duplicates removed via the Zotero trash instead of permanent deletion.
acceptanceCriteria: A duplicatas-relatorio subcommand prints, per same-content group (and per same-name, different-content group), each copy marked keep, stray or review, the owning Zotero items and their collections, and a verdict (stray, conflict, unowned, unverified) without writing to the drive or Zotero.
Bibliographic duplicates matched only by title are reported, never auto-deleted; DOI matches keep the current merge behavior.
Zotero items removed by the duplicate cleanup are sent to the Zotero trash and recorded in duplicate_actions.jsonl.

stories.title: Scan the drive once per sync run
stories.description: As the owner of a rclone-mounted library, I want one recursive PDF scan per sync so each run stops paying for the same slow directory walk several times.
acceptanceCriteria: Measured baseline recorded first: one collect_all_pdfs over 1850 PDFs took 41.5 s on the mount, and run_sync_mode currently calls it at the pre-copy preprocess, in the ambiguity check added by US-009 follow-up, and for files_to_process, besides the index builders.

A single scan result is produced early in run_sync_mode and reused by the ambiguity check, the index builders and the main loop; it is refreshed only after a step that moves or removes PDFs (preprocess, folder dedup, materialization), never speculatively.
Stale-scan safety: a file moved or deleted by an earlier step is never processed from the old list; a test covers a path removed between scan and use.

Scans per run are asserted by DriveScan unit tests with a counting wrapper; the live run is reported as a scan count. A before/after wall-time comparison on the same library was not run: the old code was not re-executed (about 15 minutes per sync).
py_compile and the test suite show no new failures versus the pre-change baseline of 17.

stories.title: Incremental Zotero library fetch
stories.description: As the owner of a large library, I want the sync to fetch only items changed since the last successful run so the full attachment and bibliographic listings (44 s and 55 s measured) are not repeated every time.
acceptanceCriteria: The last library version and a local snapshot of all non-annotation items are stored in ~/.cache/zotero_sync_webdav/library_snapshot.json and written atomically (temp file plus replace) after every successful refresh; each write is consistent with its stored version, so writing only at run end was not needed.

A refresh asks the API for items with since=<stored version> and includeTrashed=1, merges changes, drops items flagged deleted, and applies the /deleted feed for permanent deletions. includeTrashed is required: a plain since never returns trashed items (verified live).
A missing, corrupt or version-mismatched snapshot falls back to the current full fetch and says so in the log; a periodic full refresh (default weekly) bounds any drift.
Collections are still fetched fully each run (0.7 s measured).
Tests cover merge of changed items, removal through the deleted feed, and fallback on a corrupt snapshot, using fakes and no live API.
Live validation reports the item counts of an incremental run against a full fetch and they match.

stories.title: Content-hash view shared by report and sync
stories.description: As a maintainer, I want one hash-to-copies index per run so duplicate decisions stop depending on filename similarity.
acceptanceCriteria: Hashing cost is measured first: the live report hashed only 4 size-colliding candidates in under 0.1 s with a warm cache, so this story proceeds only if the sync paths that still compare by name show a real defect or cost.
If it proceeds, build_duplicates_report and the sync copy-variant and folder-dedup paths read the same index, and the story removes the duplicated comparison code it replaces.

stories.title: Make the Obsidian vault share the Drive root
stories.description: As the owner of the unified vault, I want the Obsidian collection tree to live in the same physical Drive root as the Zotero PDFs so normal sync never moves or deletes a second Obsidian copy.
acceptanceCriteria: The default Obsidian collection root resolves to the configured Zotero Drive target.
The main sync creates each collection directory once in the unified root and does not call any Obsidian-to-Drive move or duplicate-cleanup path.
The obsolete two-root ingest helper is removed rather than left as an alternate active path.
The final report describes unified-vault directories without counters for a second Obsidian copy or moved Obsidian PDFs.
Unit tests cover default root selection and directory creation without an API call or mounted Drive.
python3 -m py_compile zotero_sync_webdav.py zotero_storage_quota_audit.py and the focused unified-vault tests pass.

stories.title: Classify in-place PDFs by unified collection path
stories.description: As the owner of the unified vault, I want a PDF already under a mapped collection path to align its Zotero item to that collection without moving, copying, or renaming the file.
acceptanceCriteria: A same-content PDF in one mapped collection folder updates the parent bibliographic item to that collection using a fresh Zotero item version.
The source PDF stays at its original path and no filesystem mutation is performed by the classification step.
Duplicate filenames in multiple collection paths remain blocked from automatic collection changes.
Focused temporary-directory tests cover both the positive in-place classification and the existing ambiguity block.
python3 -m py_compile zotero_sync_webdav.py zotero_storage_quota_audit.py and the focused tests pass.
